name: Parametric Architecture
description: Design in which form is generated and controlled by algorithmic parameters and rules rather than fixed drawings. Tools like Grasshopper and Rhino let designers explore thousands of variants; Parametricism is its stylistic movement, associated with Zaha Hadid Architects and Patrik Schumacher.

name: Computational Design
description: The use of computation — scripting, optimization, machine learning — to generate, evaluate, and refine architectural form. Encompasses parametric, generative, and performance-driven design.

name: Generative Design
description: Design processes in which algorithms autonomously produce and evolve candidate solutions against goals and constraints, then the designer selects. Widely used for structural optimization and mass-customized fabrication.

name: Digital Fabrication
description: The direct production of building components from digital models via CNC milling, robotic assembly, and 3D-printed concrete or polymer. Collapses the gap between design model and physical construction.

name: Building Information Modeling
description: A shared digital model of a building's geometry and data (structure, MEP, cost, schedule) used across design, construction, and operation. Coordinates disciplines and detects clashes before construction.

name: Parametric Design
description: The design methodology underlying parametric architecture: encoding relationships and constraints into a parametric model so changes propagate through the design.

name: Vocaloid
description: Yamaha's vocal-synthesis software that sings user-written lyrics from voice databases, launched 2004. Spawned virtual singers such as Hatsune Miku and a global producer-driven music culture.

name: Vocal Synthesis
description: Synthesizing singing voices by concatenating and modifying recorded vocal samples or via neural voice models. The technical foundation of Vocaloid, speech synthesis, and AI singers.

name: Virtual Singer / Virtual Idol
description: Animated, fictional performers — Hatsune Miku, Luo Tianyi, K/DA — whose voices are synthesized and whose personas live through fan production, concerts (holograms), and media franchises.

name: Digital Audio Workstation
description: Software for recording, editing, arranging, and mixing audio and MIDI — Ableton Live, Logic Pro, FL Studio. The central tool of modern music production.

name: MIDI
description: The Musical Instrument Digital Interface (1983) — a protocol for musical instruments, controllers, and software to communicate notes and control data. Standardized electronic music-making.

name: Auto-Tune & Pitch Correction
description: Software that corrects or stylizes vocal pitch; its 1998 Auto-Tune effect became a defining sound of 2000s pop, hip-hop, and hyperpop.
